Country.evidence_source: After receiving IRB approval from The Ohio State University, participants from a regional campus were recruited from introductory and upper-level psychology classes. (Inference: The Ohio State University is located in the United States; thus the study was conducted in the United States.)

Sample.evidence_source: From the initial data set of 749 participants, 675 (367 women and 308 men) remained, and their data were analyzed. Test–retest data from 208 participants (135 women and 73 men) were gathered.

Survey method.evidence_source: Interested students signed up on the psychology department's research management website and, from there, clicked a link to a webpage that hosted the informed consent sheet. Upon providing consent, participants were directed to the survey webpage.

Percent of white in participants.evidence_source: They identified as White (79.1%), African American (11.0%), Asian American (4.1%), Latina/Latino (0.7%), Native American (0.3%), or multiracial (4.6%). ... In the test–retest subset they identified as White (81.3%), African American (8.6%), Asian American (3.4%), Latino/Latina (0.5%), Native American (0.5%), or multiracial (5.8%).

Mean age of participants.evidence_source: They ranged in age from 18 to 56 (Mage = 20.34, SD = 5.08). ... Test–retest data from 208 participants ... ranged in age from 18 to 47 (Mage = 20.27, SD = 4.53).

Percentage of college or higher of parti.evidence_source: This study was described as an investigation of body attitudes, eating habits, and well-being among college students. They were first-year college students (76.7%), sophomores (17.2%), juniors (3.7%), or seniors (1.9%). (Inference per rule: participants are undergraduate college students, thus percentage with college or higher = 100%.)

Mean BMI of participants.evidence_source: Average body mass index (BMI) was 24.21 (SD = 5.56) for women and 25.02 (SD = 5.27) for men.

Source of sample.evidence_source: Participants from a regional campus were recruited from introductory and upper-level psychology classes during three academic terms.

Assessment of BA.evidence_source: The 19 items in the BAS-2 item pool were administered.

Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: Participants reported their height in feet and inches and weight in pounds, which we used to calculate BMI: (weight × 703)/height in inches2.

section_summary.extract_value: Methods describe a single study of college students recruited from introductory and upper-level psychology classes at a regional campus of The Ohio State University, with 675 participants analyzed and a 3-week test–retest subsample of 208 participants. Measures included the BAS-2 (19-item pool), various body-image and eating-related scales, and BMI calculated from self-reported height and weight; demographic details (age, ethnicity, class year) are reported for both the full sample and the test–retest subset.

The 19 items in the BAS-2 item pool were administered. Participants reported their height in feet and inches and weight in pounds, which we used to calculate BMI.
